picks.title: The Binding of Isaac (Second Day of Rosh Hashana Torah Reading)
picks.summary: On the second day of Rosh Hashana, we read the Torah section of Genesis chapter 22 that tells the very famous and quite troubling episode of the Binding of Isaac. Abraham – the same Abraham who railed against the ways of child sacrifice of the pagans – is instructed by God to take Isaac – the same Isaac who was declared as the one who will be Abraham’s true progeny – and offer him as a sacrifice on Mount Moriah. In this podcast we attempt to understand the many connections that this reading has with the themes and ideas of Rosh Hashana.– – – – – – – – – – – – – – – – – – – – – –DONATE to TORCH
picks.reason: Detailed Torah analysis of the Binding of Isaac focusing on its spiritual and ethical meanings.

picks.summary: How can Jews with different relationships to Zionism remain bound to one another? Using history as his guide, Rabbi Cosgrove reflects on Jewish peoplehood, arguing that our future depends on sustaining a shared community capacious enough to hold disagreement without surrendering responsibility for one another.

picks.title: Chullin 132 - Ch... Ch... Changes
picks.summary:
On today’s page, Chullin 132, the rabbis debate the status of the koy, a creature caught somewhere between wild and domesticated. With Rosh Hashanah just days away, their strange animal becomes a metaphor for the struggle within each of us—and for a holiday whose very name may contain an invitation to transform ourselves. What would it take to tip the scales toward the person we want to become? Listen and find out.




Learn more about your ad choices. Visit megaphone.fm/adchoices
picks.reason: Talmudic debate uses animal metaphor to explore personal transformation for Rosh Hashanah.

picks.title: Chullin 138 - Free Bird
picks.summary:
On today’s page, Chullin 138, Maimonides and Nachmanides disagree over why the Torah commands us to send away a mother bird before taking her young. Their argument takes us from animal suffering to conservation to a deeper question about how seemingly small acts can shape our character. Can showing mercy to an animal teach us how to become more merciful ourselves? Listen and find out.


Learn more about your ad choices. Visit megaphone.fm/adchoices
picks.reason: Talmudic debate on mercy toward animals as a path to ethical character development.

picks.title: Shabbat Dinner Party V: Have the Damn Dinner
picks.summary:
On this final episode of Shabbat Dinner Party, we have the real dinner.
First, Neil Spears talks about how when we go somewhere over and over, we become known. 
Then, Gefelteria’s Jeffrey Yoskowitz and Liz Alpern put the final touches on their Shabbat dinner, and teach us about a dinnertime ritual where everyone touches the challah and we connect to break bread together. 
Finally, Kate works up the courage to have a real-life Shabbat dinner table. 
Shabbat Dinner Party is a production of Judaism Unbound. Senior Producer is Joey Taylor, and Executive Director is Miriam Terlinchamp. This episode

One goat was designated as the שעיר לה' – a sacrifice to G-d, and its blood was sprinkled in the holiest place in the world, in the inner chamber of the Bet Ha'mikdash . The other goat – the שעיר לעזאזל – was taken out into the desert, symbolically carrying all the sins of the Jewish Nation, and then thrown from a cliff.
